mindmap.label: Photosynthesis
mindmap.summary: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy, stores it as sugar, and releases oxygen. The document follows the process from light capture through the Calvin cycle to real-world applications.

children.label: Introduction
children.summary: Photosynthesis is the process plants, algae and some bacteria use to turn light into chemical energy.

children.label: Definition
children.summary: Light energy is captured and converted into chemical bonds inside the chloroplast.

children.label: Energy conversion
children.summary: Solar energy becomes chemical energy stored in carbohydrates.

children.label: Carbon fixation
children.summary: Carbon dioxide from the air is incorporated into organic molecules.

children.label: Why it matters
children.summary: Photosynthesis supplies oxygen and forms the base of most food chains on Earth.

children.label: Oxygen production
children.summary: Water splitting releases the oxygen that aerobic life depends on.

children.label: Food chains
children.summary: Organic carbon produced by photosynthesis feeds consumers.

children.label: Light Reactions
children.summary: Light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membrane and generate ATP, NADPH and oxygen.

children.label: Thylakoid membrane
children.summary: Pigments and protein complexes in the thylakoid membrane capture photons.

children.label: Electron transport
children.summary: Excited electrons move through a chain of carriers that pumps protons.

children.label: Water splitting
children.summary: Water molecules are split to replace electrons lost by chlorophyll.

children.label: Oxygen release
children.summary: Oxygen is released as a by-product of water splitting.

children.label: ATP and NADPH
children.summary: The light reactions provide the energy carriers used by the Calvin cycle.

children.label: Calvin Cycle
children.summary: The light-independent Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugar using ATP and NADPH.

children.label: Carbon fixation
children.summary: RuBisCO attaches carbon dioxide to a five-carbon sugar.

children.label: RuBisCO
children.summary: RuBisCO is the enzyme that catalyses the first step of carbon fixation.

children.label: Sugar production
children.summary: Reduction and regeneration steps produce glucose and rebuild the starting material.

children.label: Glucose
children.summary: Fixed carbon is assembled into glucose and other carbohydrates.

children.label: Chloroplast Anatomy
children.summary: The chloroplast contains the membranes and compartments where photosynthesis takes place.

children.label: Stroma
children.summary: The stroma is the fluid-filled space where the Calvin cycle runs.

children.label: Thylakoid stacks
children.summary: Stacked thylakoids increase the membrane area available for light capture.

children.label: Grana
children.summary: Grana are the stacks of thylakoid discs inside the chloroplast.

children.label: Chlorophyll
children.summary: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly blue and red wavelengths of light.

children.label: Applications
children.summary: Insights from photosynthesis research inform agriculture and renewable energy technologies.

children.label: Agriculture
children.summary: Understanding photosynthesis helps improve crop productivity.

children.label: Crop yields
children.summary: Optimising light use and carbon fixation can raise crop yields.

children.label: Renewable energy
children.summary: Artificial systems aim to mimic photosynthesis for fuel production.

children.label: Artificial photosynthesis
children.summary: Researchers design devices that use light to make chemical fuels.
